title: Bento Momentum — Asymmetric Pitch Grid
description: Asymmetric bento tiles — hero, metric, logo wall, and quote — sit on a near-black canvas with glassy surfaces and electric-blue accents. Designed for Series A founders who want a pitch deck that reads in five seconds and signals a polished, shipping product.

typography.heading: geometric sans-serif, semibold to bold weight, tight letter-spacing, optically balanced at large display sizes
typography.body: humanist sans-serif, regular weight, generous line-height suited to short single-line claims

layoutNotes: Six-column grid with 32px gutters and 48px outer margins; tiles span 1–3 columns and 1–2 rows, creating deliberate size contrast. One hero tile anchors the top-left quadrant and occupies at least twice the area of the smallest tile. All tiles share 32px inner padding, 18px rounded corners, a 1px semi-transparent border, and a subtle inner shadow for a glassy feel. Visual hierarchy flows left-to-right and large-to-small, guiding the eye from the hero claim to supporting proof points.
promptCore: Design a slide built on an asymmetric bento grid — modular tiles of deliberate size contrast on a near-black canvas with glassy surfaces and electric-accent highlights. A dominant hero tile anchors the top-left, commanding attention before the eye travels through progressively smaller proof-point tiles. The mood is a funded startup's product page, not a consulting deck: five-second readability, dark-mode confidence, every tile earning its place with one claim, one metric, or a logo wall.
goodFor: Single-stat milestone tiles displaying one large metric in 64–80px type
Logo walls of 6–12 customer or investor logos at uniform height
One-line pull quotes with an attributed speaker name beneath
Product screenshots cropped tightly to reveal a single UI moment
avoidFor: Slides with two or more paragraphs of explanatory body text
Multi-row financial tables or detailed data grids
Sequential step-by-step process flows requiring numbered order
Agenda or section-divider slides with no visual proof points
